questions.q: What is the fundamental difference between RabbitMQ and Kafka?
options: RabbitMQ is queue-first (a message is consumed once, then gone); Kafka is log-first (retained, replayable by many consumers)
They are functionally identical with different names for the same concepts
RabbitMQ retains every message forever, while Kafka deletes messages instantly after production
Kafka can only ever have one consumer per topic, unlike RabbitMQ
questions.explain: RabbitMQ's queue-first model suits task distribution; Kafka's log-first model suits replay and multiple independent readers.

questions.q: For a workload that genuinely needs "exactly one worker processes this job, then it's gone," why is RabbitMQ often a more natural fit than Kafka?
options: RabbitMQ's per-message ack/nack and dead-lettering are built directly for that task-distribution model
Kafka is technically incapable of ever being used for task distribution under any configuration
RabbitMQ is always faster than Kafka in every scenario
Kafka requires a queue product to even start up
questions.explain: Kafka's retry and error-handling patterns exist, but RabbitMQ's queue-first design is the more direct fit for pure one-worker-per-job distribution.

questions.q: How does Fabric's Eventstreams relate to Kafka, per this lesson?
options: Eventstreams is a managed, Azure-native layer that trades some configurability for near-zero ops, and can even ingest from Kafka-compatible sources
Eventstreams and Kafka have no relationship whatsoever
Eventstreams is a competing open-source project with an incompatible protocol
Eventstreams replaces the need to ever learn Kafka's own vocabulary
questions.explain: Eventstreams can ingest Kafka-compatible endpoints directly — it's a managed layer, not a separate universe from Kafka.

questions.q: How does AWS Kinesis compare to Kafka?
options: It's Kafka's closest conceptual cousin (a retained, ordered log with replay) but not wire-compatible, and it's AWS-only
Kinesis and Kafka use the identical wire protocol and are fully interchangeable
Kinesis is queue-first, exactly like RabbitMQ
Kinesis has no concept of ordering or replay at all
questions.explain: Kinesis shares Kafka's log-first shape (calling a partition a "shard"), but a Kafka client can't talk to it directly without a compatibility shim.

questions.q: According to this lesson's decision framework, when does Kafka become the right choice over its managed alternatives?
options: When you need a vendor-neutral, highly configurable, replayable log and are willing to own (or pay for) the operations
In every situation, regardless of cloud commitment or operational appetite
Only when the team has no Azure or AWS accounts at all
Only for workloads that need exactly-once task distribution
questions.explain: The lesson frames Kafka's actual niche as vendor-neutral configurability at the cost of owning the operations yourself.
